title: API Token Controls
scope: Admin controls, logging and revocation for API credentials on SaaS platforms. Sourced from vendor documentation; not an audit of any tenant.

definitions.conditional: Documented, with plan, policy or endpoint conditions.
definitions.excluded: The named control explicitly does not cover this credential.
definitions.not_supported: Vendor documentation states this credential lacks the control.
definitions.unknown: No source found either way. Not a negative finding.
definitions.not_verified: No source found either way. Not a negative finding.
definitions.not_applicable: Does not apply to this credential.
definitions.limited: Documented for a narrower case only.

providers.name: MongoDB Atlas
providers.scope_notes: Atlas cloud service; Admin API credentials (service accounts, legacy API keys) manage Atlas but cannot read cluster data, while database users read data; database auditing, access history and workload federation need dedicated (M10+) clusters.

controls.name: Temporary User
controls.what: Database user is deleted automatically after 6 hours, 1 day or 1 week.
controls.setting: Database & Network Access > Add New Database User > Temporary User

controls.name: Restrict access to specific clusters
controls.what: Limits a database user to chosen clusters and federated database instances.
controls.setting: Database user > Restrict Access to Specific Clusters

controls.name: Project IP access list
controls.what: Only listed IPs can connect to clusters.
controls.setting: Database & Network Access > IP Access List

controls.name: Delete database user
controls.what: Removes the database user; also the only way to revoke an X.509 user.
controls.setting: Database & Network Access > Database Users > Delete

controls.name: Roles required to add database users
controls.what: Only users with the listed Organization or Project roles can create database users of any authentication type.

controls_unknown: Whether an org can block creation of legacy API keys entirely.
Whether API keys have any expiry setting.
Whether deleting a service account or secret invalidates already-issued 1-hour access tokens.
Whether deleting a database user terminates open connections.
Whether Admin API read (GET) calls are recorded anywhere; Activity Feed documents changes, not reads.
Default secret expiration value for service accounts.

authentication.summary: Username and password authenticate a driver or shell directly to the cluster. These are separate from Atlas (UI) users and read/write data.

federation.details: Database-level credential; Atlas UI SSO does not govern it.

ip_restriction.boundary: Project IP access list (or private endpoints/peering) gates every client connection to the cluster; not per user.

lifetime.summary: Permanent unless created as temporary user (6 h, 1 day, 1 week)

renewal.expiry_basis: Password has no documented expiry; temporary users are deleted at end of duration.

administration.summary: Created via UI, Atlas CLI or Admin API; roles and cluster restrictions limit scope.
administration.conditions: Admin API credentials with the right project role can create database users.

offboard.details: Database users are separate from Atlas users, so removing an Atlas user does not touch them.

inventory.details: GET /api/atlas/v2/groups/{groupId}/databaseUsers lists all database users in a project (per project, not org-wide).

disable.ui: Project > Security > Project Identity & Access > Users: limit Project Owner / Project Database Access Admin roles (only these, plus Org Owner and Stream Processing admin roles, can add database users)

usage.ui: Project > Database > Clusters > cluster ... menu > View Database Access History (7 days, by username)

reads.ui: Project > Security > Database & Network Access > Advanced > Database Auditing On > select authCheck Reads with Successes and Failures; then Clusters > ... > Download Logs > mongodb-audit-log, search atype "authCheck"
reads.cli: atlas auditing update; atlas logs download <hostname> mongodb-audit-log.gz

log_sources.name: Database Access History
log_sources.notes: M10+; successful and failed auth attempts, last 7 days.

log_sources.name: Database audit log (mongodb-audit-log.gz)
log_sources.notes: Not on Free/Flex; authenticate and authCheck actions; logs kept 30 days; download or push export.

lifecycle_events.notes: Audit log atype; reads need authChecksReadAll to log successes

anomaly_cues: Database user created by API key

containment.steps: Delete the user or change its password; tighten project IP access list.
containment.notes: Docs say clients lose access once the user is deleted; open sessions not addressed.

unknown: Whether open connections are dropped on delete

calls.log_notes: Auth logged in Database Access History (M10+); command itself not documented
Only if database auditing enabled with read successes (authChecksReadAll); not on Free/Flex
